To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we reconstructed and model metabolic networks for ancient enterobacteria and identified ancient metabolic capacities and evolutionary trends.

(1) ancestral metabolic models of enteric bacteria are a novel approach to infer the metabolic capacity of ancient microbes; (2) ancestral metabolic models can identify conserved catabolic phenotypic traits and predict metabolic capabilities of ancient microbes; and (3) the ancestral models can be validated against experimental data and are useful for identification of targets for antimicrobial drug development.
ancestral enterobacteria had the capacity to use a wide variety of carbon sources, including sugars, amino acids, organic acids, and polymeric carbon sources such as chitin and starch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the metabolic evolution of the enterobacterial family, and how this evolution relates to the evolution of the family's phenotypes and lifestyles.
the evolution of metabolic networks in a group of organisms, the Enterobacteriaceae, that are of great importance to human health, agriculture, and biotechnology.
the study of metabolic evolution in a group of bacteria that are among the most abundant and important microorganisms on Earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our study provides a framework for understanding metabolic network evolution and adaptation in enterobacteria, and that our ancestral metabolic models can be used to identify novel drug targets in enterobacterial pathogens.
the ancestral enterobacteria were able to grow on all carbon sources that we have tested, and that the ability to grow anaerobically is an ancestral feature of the enterobacterial lineage.

our study shows that metabolic network evolution has occurred in the enterobacteria, but the extent to which it has is not yet clear, and that this evolution is likely to have been driven by adaptation to the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have used ancestral metabolic models to investigate metabolism of the ancient enterobacterial ancestor and evolution of the network.

ancestral core metabolic models provide an opportunity to investigate the metabolism of ancient micro-organisms, and can be used to identify conserved and differentiable phenotypes that may be useful for understanding the evolution of enterobacteria and other bacteria, and to identify new targets for control of infectious diseases caused by these organisms.

the ancestral enterobacteria were capable of aerobic respiration, fermentation, anaerobic respiration, and anaerobic fermentation, and that the ancestral enteric core metabolic model is capable of growth on a wide variety of carbon sources, but not on some amino acids and nucleotides, and that the enterobacteria have evolved the ability to utilize more carbon sources over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ancestral enterobacterial metabolism was likely more versatile than that of extant free-living enterics, which may reflect the more diverse and nutrient-rich environment in the past.
metabolic network models of ancient organisms are feasible, and can provide insights into the evolution of metabolic capabilities of ancient organisms.
ancestral metabolic models can be used to infer ancient phenotypes and to understand the evolution of metabolism in the Enterobacteriaceae.
